title: A finite intermediate integral ring has a conductor power
statement: Let B be a Noetherian semilocal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension 1 [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] with Jacobson radical m_B, let K be its fraction field, and let A be a finite B-algebra contained in K. If A and B have the same fraction field, then there exists an integer n>0 such that m_B^n A is contained in B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 proof, paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: Let M=A/B be the quotient of the finite B-module A by the image of B. The quotient of a finite module is finite. The inclusion A into K and the equality Frac(A)=Frac(B)=K identify the localization of M at the generic prime (0) with zero: every element of A/B becomes zero after inverting a nonzero element of B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 (lemma-semi-local-dimension-one-conductor), proof paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: Every prime in the support of M is therefore nonzero. Because B is a one-dimensional domain, every nonzero prime is maximal. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], the support is the zero locus V(J) of the annihilator J=Ann_B(M), so every prime containing J is a maximal ideal (not every maximal ideal need contain J). By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], the radical of J is the intersection of the primes in V(J) (the whole ring B if V(J) is empty); an intersection of some maximal ideals contains the intersection of all of them, which is the Jacobson radical m_B. Hence m_B is contained in the radical of J. The ideal m_B is finitely generated because B is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] therefore gives n>0 with m_B^n contained in J, equivalently m_B^n M=0.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N2 (lemma-semi-local-dimension-one-conductor), proof paragraph beginning 'Since the fraction fields of B and A are the same'

proof.text: The equality m_B^n M=0 says that the image of every element of m_B^n A in A/B is zero. Thus m_B^n A is contained in B, as required.
